description:
Advances: ancora.derive, ancora.parsing

Ready-for: implement

Severity: Medium

Symptom:
TagScanner collapses two tests named works under different describe blocks when both carry alpha.value, returning one tag entry instead of two. Folding alpha.group.value produces alpha.group.value and alpha.group, but not its actual owning subject alpha. Gate then matches these folded keys to subject ids. Whole-file derivation can mask both losses today; precise test-level attribution must preserve each test and use authored requirement ownership.

Evidence:
Current main 82c2ca8. Reproducible probe and output: /tmp/ancora-friction-probe.exs and /tmp/ancora-friction-probe.log, copied into the agent-adoption-friction investigation under /Users/mz/Documents/my-vault/LLMs/investigations/ancora/2026-09-07-agent-adoption-friction. Measurements duplicate_test_names and nested_requirement_fold. Source: lib/ancora/tag_scanner.ex dedupe_key/1 and parent_id/1; lib/ancora/gate.ex subject_files/2.

Why now:
Correcting false cross-subject drift requires retaining test identity. Reusing the existing lossy tag/file map would exchange false positives for missing bindings. This is a prerequisite of the test-attribution investigation, not a request for adopters to rename tests or flatten requirement ids.

Suspected cause:
Identity uses display name rather than lexical test occurrence; ownership is inferred by removing an id segment instead of consulting the parsed subject requirement lists.

## Investigation contract, 2026-09-07

Evidence and corrections:
Report: /Users/mz/Documents/my-vault/LLMs/investigations/ancora/2026-09-07-agent-adoption-friction/04-report.md
Measurements: /Users/mz/Documents/my-vault/LLMs/investigations/ancora/2026-09-07-agent-adoption-friction/03-measurements.md
Source revision: 82c2ca8329e1303ececc610dfc9f72986b96c84a. This contract proposes work; no implementation is claimed.

Deliverable:
Preserve each literal tagged test carrier with per-side identity consisting of project-relative file, lexical module, describe ancestry and AST occurrence. Display names are not unique identifiers. Resolve requirement ownership from the index's authored requirement lists; retain direct subject tags. Do not infer ownership by trimming dotted identifiers. Expose the resulting carrier-to-subject mapping to Gate and other scanner consumers. Keep unknown and ambiguous IDs subject to existing index diagnostics. Preserve inherited module/describe tags and static for-comprehension carriers without evaluating them.

Verification:
- The saved duplicate_test_names fixture yields exactly two distinct carriers, both belonging to alpha; alpha.group.value maps to actual owner alpha, without fabricating alpha.group ownership.
- Include identical names across modules, repeated requirements, inherited tags, generated static carriers and unknown IDs. Moving or formatting a carrier must preserve its derived binding set; cross-diff borrowed-tag identity policy is separate.
- Run scanner/index/Gate focused tests and an end-to-end fixture showing both carriers contribute their different production calls.
- Cadence: focused tests during implementation; at final verification run mix compile --warnings-as-errors, mix test, mix format --check-formatted, mix deps.unlock --check-unused and mix spec.check against the actual integration base. CI must pass both configured Elixir/OTP combinations. Record evidence of the described symptom after the consuming release before claiming it done.

Allowed touches:
lib/ancora/tag_scanner.ex, lib/ancora/index.ex, scanner consumers in lib/ancora/{gate,status,review}.ex, relevant tests and ancora.parsing/derive specs and listed decisions.

Out of Scope (files):
Unrelated production modules, credentials, dependencies and consumer repositories. Release metadata belongs to release preparation.

Out of Scope (intent):
No resolver reachability implementation, test-name restrictions, requirement-ID migration or borrowed-tag rename policy change.

Merge gate:
- [ ] Focused negative and positive behavior fixtures pass.
- [ ] Affected specs and decisions describe the actual changed behavior.
- [ ] Full repository CI and spec gate pass without cosmetic acknowledgment edits.

Decision:
Keep lexical identity until attribution and use authored ownership. The probe demonstrates that existing display-name deduplication and dotted-prefix folding both lose information.

Open Questions:
None. Unmeasured consumer replay and release behavior are explicit Verification obligations, not claimed results.
